references.note: Approved disc, lighting and camera; do not copy its creature.
Native species shape: huge orc, dragon-skull helm, raised two-handed greatsword, dark green-black plate.
Shipped catalog humanoid/orc: hammer + shield, gold-trimmed armour. Massok/Krogar must stay distinct from this and from each other.

prompt_fields.subject: A huge, heavily armoured orc warrior wearing a dragon skull as a helm, its bone jaw framing the orc's face and pale horns curving up from the sides. He grips a massive two-handed sword raised diagonally across his body, dark green-black plate armour with jagged pauldrons. The two-handed greatsword is held upright and close against his body, angled only slightly, and is drawn SHORT: the blade tip ends below the top of the horned skull helm, well inside the disc. The sword must be fully contained within the disc.
prompt_fields.contrast: Third humanoid/orc catalog identity (with golbug the hammer-and-shield destroyer and brotoq the dual-axe reaver already shipped, and Krogar shipping in the same handoff group). Massok's dragon-skull helm and single massive raised greatsword must read as a clearly different silhouette from golbug (hammer+shield) and brotoq (dual axes) -- no shield, no dual weapons, a distinctive pale bone-helm silhouette breaking up the dark armour read. Silhouette (dragon-skull helm + single raised greatsword) and value (pale bone helm against dark green-black armour) are the anchors.
prompt_fields.composition: One compact complete creature on a single circular tabletop disc, steep overhead three-quarter camera; visible clear neutral base ring on every side. Keep all anatomy and equipment well inside the inner four-fifths of disc radius. Base brightness must visually match reference neutral disc, with no illumination spill or ground effects. Base-plate discipline, calibrated from monster-batch-d/monster-batch-e on this same style reference: an initial 8-unit-darker disc instruction overshot to base_drift -9 to -15 on several fresh generations, while a follow-up 4-unit-darker instruction landed cleanly inside the +-8 tolerance on a controlled retest (-5.11). Render the neutral disc -- including the whole outer-sixth ring band -- only about 4 RGB luminance units darker than the style reference's disc appears at first read: a small, conservative undershoot, not a full shade darker. Do not darken the creature itself to compensate -- only the disc plate takes this small intentional downward bias. Add no warm cast, glow, bounce-light, gradient or vignette to the disc anywhere, including directly under or behind dark-bodied creatures. HARD LIMIT: the sword blade tip, pauldron spikes and horn tips must all end inside the inner four-fifths of the disc radius; no part of the sword may reach or cross the disc rim (a previous attempt swung a long diagonal blade beyond the disc edge at radius 1.20). Shrink the figure slightly and keep the sword short, held compactly.
prompt_fields.palette: Dark green-black plate armour with jagged metal pauldrons, a pale bone-white dragon skull helm with visible curved horns as the dominant value break, dull grey greatsword blade; dry neutral charcoal disc with restrained copper-grey bevel, kept a visibly lighter value than the creature's armour so the two never merge.
